title: Validator Diagnostic Codes
intro: Generated from `validator-diagnostic-codes.json`; edit the JSON and run `npm run generate:diagnostic-registry`. The same command also syncs the editor extension copy at `extensions/aoe2-ai-parser-extension/data/diagnostic-codes.json`.
This is the registry for `aoe2_ai_lab` lint and package-integrity issue codes.
Use it when triaging `lint --json`, `lint-package --json`, Markdown reports, or VS Code/Cursor diagnostics.
Severity is the default validator severity. Confidence is per occurrence: `definite` for definitely reachable code and `conditional` when the finding is inside an unknown preprocessor branch.
Editor actions describe the current local VS Code/Cursor extension behavior:
- `quick fix`: an edit action may be offered.
- `explain`: a non-editing explanation action may be offered.
- `none`: no code action is currently wired.
profile_suppression_note: Manual `--suppress-code <code>` can suppress any finding code for one lint run. Package-integrity codes are not suppressible through linter profile suppression.

codes.meaning: `set-goal` is missing either the goal id or value.
A local `class-*` constant aliases a documented built-in class id or built-in class symbol. Prefer the built-in name.
A command argument does not match a known registry parameter family. This can be a real bug or a registry coverage gap.
A command argument is in a direct id slot but its symbol name strongly suggests a different family, such as an `sn-*` strategic number in a `GoalId` slot.
A literal numeric command argument or resolved integer `defconst` is outside an explicit documented range for that parameter, such as `0` in a `GoalId` slot documented as `1 to 16000`.
A schema-validated command has the wrong number of arguments.
A long single-line `defrule` is risky because DE can reject it unpredictably even when the repo parser accepts it. Expand the rule across multiple lines.
A command documented as Fact/Action/FactAction is used in the wrong rule side or nested context.
A `typeOp` slot received a math/compare operator such as `g:=` instead of a plain type prefix such as `g:`.
A valid typed prefix or typed operator is followed by an operand whose name strongly suggests a different type, such as `g:` or `g:=` before an `sn-*` strategic number.
A `defrule` closed without an `=>` separator.
A set of `defconst` aliases forms a cycle, so the constants cannot resolve to a numeric value.

A numeric `defconst` value is outside the observed signed 32-bit range of -2147483648 to 2147483647. AoE2 DE validated one-step overflow values as loading but clamping to the nearest signed-32 boundary.
One `#load-if-defined` or `#load-if-not-defined` block contains more than one `#else`.
Multiple `.ai` files resolve to the same root `.per`. This can be intentional for personalities but should be explicit.
Multiple `.ai` files have the same case-insensitive display name. This can confuse package users and launcher/editor selection.
One `.ai` file loads the same resolved `.per` root more than once. This may be intentional, but it usually indicates a redundant or mistaken package manifest entry.
One reachable `.per` file includes the same resolved `.xs` file more than once. This may be intentional when relying on top-level XS side effects, but is usually redundant.
One reachable `.per` file loads the same resolved `.per` file more than once. This may be intentional, but usually indicates a redundant or mistaken load directive.
Multiple `.per` files have the same case-insensitive basename. This is legal in subfolders, but it can confuse package review, load-target completion, and human navigation.
A definitely active file assigns two different parsed values to the same `defconst` name.
A rule has no actions after `=>`.
A rule has no facts before `=>`.
An AI `include` directive has a quoted target that does not include the required `.xs` file extension.
Livestock targeting uses `action-default` where `action-move` is usually expected.
A logical operator has the wrong number of direct child facts. `not` expects one child fact; binary operators such as `and` and `or` expect two.
The reachable load graph cycles back to an already-active `.per` file.
The reachable load graph exceeds the documented maximum nested load depth of 10.
A preprocessor directive has invalid syntax, such as a missing condition token.
`#load-if-defined` and `#load-if-not-defined` conditionals are nested more than the documented maximum of 50 levels.
A `defconst` declaration is structurally invalid, such as a missing name, missing value, unterminated quoted text value, or multiple unquoted value tokens.
An `include` directive is structurally invalid, usually because its target is not quoted.
A `load` or `#load` directive is structurally invalid, usually because its target is not quoted.
A `load-random` directive has a structurally invalid entry. Entries should be an optional weight followed by a quoted target.
A `load-random` entry uses a `+` weight form. AIRef documents this as UserPatch syntax and notes uncertain or bugged DE behavior.
A reachable `.per` file has a `load` or `load-random` directive after an `include` directive. AIRef documents that load directives should be placed before include directives.
An `(include "...")` target could not be resolved.
A `(load "...")` or `#load` target could not be resolved.
A symbol is known from archived AIRef/game-string data, but is not marked as DE-compatible in the local DE reference registry.
A raw `#load` directive appears in an installed `.per`; assemble components before install.
A local `defconst` redefines a documented built-in class constant by the same name.
A chat action may repeat every rule pass because the rule is not disabled or guarded.
A rule exceeds DE's 32 element limit for facts/actions/logical operators.
A typed comparison was split, such as `< g:` instead of `g:<`.
A site-specific train-target alias is not a built-in identifier in DE and must be declared with its required `defconst` value before direct `can-train` or `train` use.
A site-specific train-target alias appears after `c:` but is not known as a built-in typed constant; declare its required `defconst` value before using it in DUC train actions.
A source line exceeds the documented 255-character AI script line limit, including comments.
An `.ai` file did not resolve to any root `.per`.
Parentheses close too early or the file is missing closing parentheses.
A value after `c:` is not a known built-in, documented value, or reachable `defconst`.
A symbol is locally validated for some train contexts but is not validated as an `up-target-point ... action-train c:` target.
A symbol is known in local validation notes, but is not validated for the current direct or dynamic train-target context.
A token looks like an AoE identifier but is not known in reachable constants or local reference data.
A position token used by `up-get-point` is not a built-in or reachable `defconst`.
A strategic-number token is not in the local DE SN registry or reachable constants.
`#else` appears without a matching active preprocessor conditional.
`#end-if` appears without a matching active preprocessor conditional.
A `.per` file exists in the package but is not reachable from any resolved `.ai` root.
A command writes a block of goals too low in the goal range; use safer higher goals.
`up-set-target-object` reads a search list before retained search evidence proves that list was rebuilt.
A DUC target command runs without retained evidence that local target objects exist.
An XS function is known to be rejected by the AoE2 DE AI XS parser.
`xs-script-call` targets an included XS function that has one or more parameters. AI scripts can only call zero-parameter XS functions.
A new `defrule` starts before the previous one closed.
A preprocessor conditional is missing its matching `#end-if`.
`up-build place-point` uses the current target point; its third argument is still escrow state, not a coordinate.
`up-can-build` uses literal `0` for escrow state; project scripts should prefer a named `without-escrow` goal.

triage_notes: Start package triage from top-level `issue_groups` in `lint-package --json`.
Treat `command-argument-mismatch`, `unsafe-set-target-object`, and `unscoped-duc-target` as review prompts unless the surrounding script context clearly proves a bug.
Treat `stale-ai-root` as a package failure by default.
Treat `duplicate-root-target` as warning-level package hygiene; community AI personalities can intentionally share a root script.
Treat `unreachable-per-file` as info unless you are pruning package files or enforcing a release package.
